fields: Contact Name And Title For Public
pending form: Current Status (e.g. 'In Review'), SubVersionID, Public Contact Phone Number
fills_event_fields: event_type (Nature of Incident: 'Authorized Wet Weather CSO Overflow', 'Discharged untreated sewage', 'Discharged partially treated ... effluent', 'Other')
source_status (pending vs reviewed table; nForm 'Current Status')

cadence: Law: report to DEC and local health officer within 12 hours of discovery; end time and volume amended within three business days if unknown. Reviewed rows appear after DEC staff review (days to weeks; some pending rows from 12/28/2025 were still 'In Review' on 11/01/2026).
history: DEC: 'There is no data available prior to January 1, 2007.' 2007 range returned 45 incident rows; CSO table populated from 2016. Per-year counts (CSO reports / other reports): 2016 117/30, 2019 213/71, 2023 112/90, 2024 206/65, 2025 172/55, 2026 (to Nov 1) 115/33. Archive = same page with an older date range.

access_detail: ASP.NET WebForms page. GET returns the last ~30 days (TextBoxDateBegin defaults to one month back). sample_record.Location Description: CSO – 06: (Bay Street – south of CVPS) CSO – 14: (Mill Street)

fills_event_fields: published_at (posted immediately on submission, per DEC)
cadence: Operator-entered in real time. Law: alert 'as soon as possible, but no longer than one hour from discovery' (four hours if no phone/internet at the site). DEC: 'Once submitted, the Public Alert will be immediately available for public viewing'. Observed latencies 2026: Vergennes CSO#002 began 9:00 pm 4/16, alert 9:33 pm; Burlington Park St CSO began 5:02 pm 8/8, alert 6:11 pm; Montpelier CSOs began ~5:35 pm 6/10, alert 6:11 am 6/11; St Johnsbury CSO-06 began 10:55 pm 10/13, alert 9:41 am 10/14 (discovery time is not published, so whether a deadline was missed cannot be judged).
history: Alerts from 2016 (Act 86 effective May 4, 2016); 49 alerts in 2016, 191 in 2019, 125 in 2024, 114 in 2025, 94 in 2026 to Nov 1. Alert IDs reach 4300 (Oct 2026).
license: Page footer: "Copyright © 2025 State of Vermont. All rights reserved" with links to Accessibility Policy and Privacy Policy. No data licence stated on the WWInventory pages. (Public record under 10 V.S.A. § 1295; ANR open data elsewhere is under the Vermont Open Geodata Policy v1.1.)
status_reason: The only near-real-time statewide sewage alert feed in NH/VT; carries outfall names and receiving water; no API so it must be scraped by POST.

name: RSA 485-A:13, I(c) - notice of bypass or upset to downstream water systems
access_detail: Merged chapter page fetched (raw/nh-rsa-485A.html).
legal_basis: RSA 485-A:13, I(c): "Any person responsible for a bypass or upset at a wastewater facility shall give immediate notice of the bypass or upset to all public or privately owned water systems drawing water from the same receiving water and located within 20 miles downstream of the point of discharge. The permittee shall maintain a list of persons, and their telephone numbers, who are to be notified immediately by telephone. In addition, written notification, which shall be postmarked within 3 days of the bypass or upset, shall be sent to such persons." Source note for 485-A:13: 1989, 339:1. 1990, 248:3. 1996, 228:108.
status_reason: Only NH statute requiring notice of a sewage release; it runs to downstream water systems, not the public, and does not cover CSOs as such.
notes: RSA 485-A:2 defines "Bypass" as "the intentional diversion of waste streams from any portion of the wastewater facilities."

name: RSA 485-A:8, II-III - CSO temporary partial use areas; criteria apply during CSO and up to 3 days after
legal_basis: RSA 485-A:8, II: class B waters "shall be considered as being acceptable for fishing, swimming and other recreational purposes ... Where it is demonstrated ... that the class B criteria cannot reasonably be met in certain surface waters at all times as a result of combined sewer overflow events, temporary partial use areas shall be established by rules ..." III: partial-use criteria "shall apply during combined sewer overflow discharges and up to 3 days following cessation of said discharge."
status_reason: Gives NH's statutory 3-day post-CSO window (useful context, not a public-notice rule).

name: Env-Wq 1108.14 Water Quality Standards for Designated Beaches (Env-Wq 1100 Public Bathing Places)
legal_basis: Designated beach "unsafe for public use" if the single-sample standard "is exceeded by 70 counts in any one sample or by any amount in 2 or more samples taken during the same sampling event" or the geometric-mean standard "is exceeded in 3 samples over a 60-day period." Freshwater: E. coli >88 counts/100 mL single, geometric mean 47. Saltwater: Enterococci >104 single, geometric mean 35. On exceedance the owner shall "Retest for bacteria" and "Post a bacteria advisory provided by the department." Cyanobacteria advisory when scum is dominant (>50% of algal cell count) or total cyanobacteria >70,000 cells/mL.
status_reason: Defines when NH beach advisories are issued.
